en.headline: Police treat Diamond Hill knife case as attempted robbery
en.dek: HK01 reported that a woman demanded Octopus cards and HK$100 notes at the station counter on Sunday, and was arrested early Monday on suspicion of attempted robbery.
body: Police are treating Sunday evening's Diamond Hill station incident as an attempted robbery, a development beyond the earlier report of a woman striking a counter with a knife.

HK01 reported that officers received a call at about 6:50pm on Sunday from staff at the Diamond Hill station customer service centre. The report said a woman pointed a knife at staff, demanded Octopus cards and HK$100 notes, struck the counter glass with the knife, and left without taking anything. Officers later found a broken ceramic blade about 5 centimetres long at the station, the report said.

The same report said police traced the woman to Ching Wai House at Tsz Ching Estate in Tsz Wan Shan and arrested a 50-year-old woman shortly before 2am on Monday on suspicion of attempted robbery. She was detained for investigation. Bastille Post reported that firefighters forced entry to a fourth-floor flat around 1am and that the woman was taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital. She has not been charged. The woman has not been named here.

zh.headline: 警方將鑽石山持刀案列作企圖行劫
zh.dek: 《香港01》引述，星期日傍晚一名女子在鑽石山站客務中心持刀索取八達通卡及100元紙幣，星期一凌晨以涉嫌企圖行劫被捕。
body: 鑽石山站星期日傍晚的持刀事件，警方現列作企圖行劫處理。這是早前報稱女子持刀敲打櫃柱之後的新發展。
《香港01》報道，警方星期日約下午6時50分接獲港鐵鑽石山站客務中心職員報案，指一名女子持刀指嚇職員，要求交出八達通卡及100元港幣紙幣，並用刀敲打櫃柱玻璃，未取得財物便離開。報道又說，警方其後在站內檢獲一塊長約5厘米的斷裂陶瓷刀片。
同報報道，警方循閉路電視追查至慈雲山慈正邨正暉樓，星期一凌晨近2時拘捕一名50歲女子，她涉嫌企圖行劫，現正被扣留調查。《巴士的報》則報道，消防約凌晨1時破門進入四樓一個單位，女子其後被送往伊利沙伯醫院。她尚未被落案起訴。本文不刊出她的姓名。
